title: ChatContact/changes maxChanges=0 regresses newState below oldState
description:
In ChatContactChangesHandler::call() (crates/kith-chat/src/contact.rs), when a client sends maxChanges=0 and at least one change is pending, the truncation branch executes:

  let truncated = &added_with_counter[..0]; // empty slice
  let last_counter = truncated.last().map(|(_, c)| *c).unwrap_or(0); // 0
  (truncated.to_vec(), true, format!("s-{last_counter}"))  // "s-0"

This sets newState="s-0" regardless of sinceState. If sinceState is "s-2" (client already synced to s-2), the response returns newState="s-0" which is less than sinceState. RFC 8620 §5.6 requires that newState >= oldState in all cases, including the truncation path.

Consequence: the client regresses to s-0 and re-fetches changes it has already seen, producing duplicate-delivery of contacts.

Root cause: when the truncated slice is empty, last_counter falls back to 0 via unwrap_or(0) instead of using since_counter as the floor.

Fix: when the truncated slice is empty (maxChanges=0 case), newState should be oldState (sinceState) since no progress was made. Alternative: reject maxChanges=0 as invalid at parse time before any store access. Either way, newState must never go below sinceState.

No existing test covers maxChanges=0. A test with sinceState="s-2", 1 change pending, maxChanges=0 would catch this.
